pll2d6c4-d1e3514.summary: States that as among good angels some rule others, among bad angels some are over others; while the world lasts angels rule angels, humans humans, demons demons, but in the future all rule will cease. Demons rule by greater or lesser knowledge, over a province, a person, or a vice ('spirit of pride'). Riches are called mammon, a demon's name, not because the devil gives or takes riches but because he uses them to tempt and deceive.
claims: All prelacy ends in the future.
The devil uses riches to tempt.

pl-l2d6c4.summary: Notes that as among good angels some rule others, so among bad angels some are set over others; while the world lasts angels rule angels, humans humans, and demons demons, but in the future all rule will cease. Demons have greater or lesser rule by their knowledge: some over a province, a person, or a vice, hence 'spirit of pride' or 'of lust.' Riches are called by a demon's name, mammon, not because the devil can give or take riches but because he uses them to tempt and deceive.
claims: Among demons, as among angels, some rule others.
All rule among creatures will cease in the future.
Demons rule in proportion to their knowledge, over provinces, persons, or vices.
Demons are named from the vices they tempt to.
The devil does not control riches but uses them to tempt.
